## Donor factor across seams: raw copy (`limiter`) {#sec-ch03-thetacopy}

The tracer flux positivity limiter of @sec-ch08-theta computes, per cell and species, a factor $\Theta\in[0,1]$ and scales
every face flux that drains the cell by it. The limited flux of a face must be one number on both sides, or the mass
removed from the donor is not the mass added to the receiver. At a block seam one side's donor is a ghost, so that
ghost must hold the donor's own $\Theta$[^rg-f9864f25fc41]. On a cubed sphere an interpolated ghost would be a blend of several cells'
factors, not the donor's; the exchange therefore uses `interpolate(false)`. The species enthalpy that the withheld
mass carries is exchanged the same way, so the carry of a shared face also uses the donor's own value.

Local symbols: $\mathcal F_f$ the requested species flux through face $f$ before limiting
[kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$]; $i_{\mathrm{dn}}(f)$ the index of the donor cell of face $f$, the upwind cell the flux drains.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The positivity limiter's donor factor $\Theta$ is exchanged into ghost cells as a raw, index-matched copy,
never interpolated, so both blocks sharing a face scale its flux by the donor's own factor
(@eq-ch03-thetacopy-face).

**Data.** In/out: $\Theta\in[0,1]$ [-] per cell and species, ghosts included, and, when species carry energy, the
species enthalpy [J kg$^{-1}$], copied the same way.

**Placement.** Each stage, inside `PositivityLimiter::apply`: after $\Theta$ and its census, before the carry and
the scaling of the fluxes.

**Activation.** Hydro: at least one species (`ny` > 0) and either `dynamics.equation-of-state.limiter` on or
face-flux covariance rows on the $x_2$ or $x_3$ faces (`cov2`, `cov3`). Scalars: the limiter on or the scalar's own
covariance row (`cov`), with no species condition.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact copy; species mass conserved across seams.

**Evidence.** `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python`, `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_moist_python`,
`test_sedimentation_cubed_seam` (pass at the pin); check `[C12]`.
:::

### Derivation

See @sec-ch08-theta for donor scaling and its conservation requirement. This section needs only its interface, as
in `sources/canoe__theta_seam_TECH_REPORT.md` §1 and §6: the limited flux of face $f$ is

$$
\mathcal F^{\Theta}_f = \Theta_{i_{\mathrm{dn}}(f)}\,\mathcal F_f,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thetacopy-face}

and the two blocks sharing $f$ each evaluate $\Theta_{i_{\mathrm{dn}}(f)}$, one from its interior and one from its ghost, so the
ghost must hold the donor's value bit for bit. A raw copy delivers exactly the neighbour's interior cell that occupies
the ghost position, after the same reverse, flip and transpose relabelling as every cubed-sphere strip; within a panel
and across $x_1$ seams the ghost is the same cell anyway. The factor of each face, @eq-ch03-thetacopy-face, is
`flux_positivity_factor` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_factor >}}), applied to the register
rows in `post_` after the copy ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::post_ >}}).
Nothing is approximated. The check confirms the copy (`[C12]`): over $2\times10^5$ random faces a copied $\Theta$
leaves a column residual of exactly zero at every one of them.[^tc-c12]

[^tc-c12]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C12]`; a numpy and sympy port of the donor-factor exchange and the donor scaling of the limited
    flux (at 73c45a7c `flux_positivity_factor` in `PositivityLimiter::post_`), CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

$\Theta$ is a cell quantity per species, computed in each stage after the $x_1$ seam fluxes are made single-valued
(@sec-ch03-x1seams) and before the fluxes are scaled. Its ghosts are filled like conserved-variable ghosts: the
exchange at internal faces (corners as in @sec-ch03-exchange), then every installed bfunc in scalar mode at physical
faces. The hydro and the scalar module share one driver, `PositivityLimiter`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp PositivityLimiter >}}): `apply` computes $\Theta$, books its census on the
interior cells, fills the ghosts with `sync_`, then carries and scales in `post_`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::apply >}}).

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| gate (hydro) | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `PositivityLimiter` | `limiter`, or covariance rows (`cov2`, `cov3`) |
| the driver | {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::apply >}} | `apply` | none |
| ghost fill of $\Theta$ and the enthalpy | {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::sync_ >}} | `sync_` | none |
| raw copy and bfunc fill | {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_sync_theta_ >}} | `interpolate` | none |
| gate (scalar) | {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}} | `flux_positivity_sync_theta_` | `limiter`, or the scalar's covariance row (`cov`) |

: Code map of the donor-factor copy. {#tbl-ch03-thetacopy-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-thetacopy-code):

1. With `ny` > 0 and either the limiter on or face-flux covariance rows added on the $x_2$ or $x_3$ faces
   (`cov2`, `cov3`: those rows can export tracer a cell does not hold), the hydro fills `PositivityInputs`, with
   `species_enthalpy` and the donor velocities when species carry energy, and calls `PositivityLimiter::apply`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. `theta` computes $\Theta$ with `flux_positivity_theta` and `census_` books its meters
   ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::theta >}}).
3. `sync_` exchanges $\Theta$ under `hydro_theta`, and the enthalpy under `hydro_hspec`, each through
   `flux_positivity_sync_theta_` with `interpolate(false)` and `type(kScalar)`, then each installed bfunc fills it at
   physical faces ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_sync_theta_ >}}).
4. `post_` keeps the withheld mass's energy and momentum with `flux_positivity_carry_` and scales the register rows
   by `flux_positivity_factor` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::post_ >}}).
5. The scalar fills its own factor the same way, under `scalar_theta`, and runs the shared limiter
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** The copy runs whenever $\Theta$ is computed: with species (`ny` > 0) and either the limiter on or a
face-flux covariance row added on $x_2$ or $x_3$. The covariance is on by default (@sec-ch03-facemoments), so a run
with species can take this path without `limiter: true`. Use this fragment in a moist deck such as `bryan.yaml`,
which already sets `limiter: true`:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `equation-of-state`[^rg-970cd699212d].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-moist, limiter: true}   # or keep the default false and the covariance rows
```

Nothing is refused. The raw copy and the fill are
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_sync_theta_ >}}):

```cpp
  Variables tvars;
  tvars[key] = theta;
  SyncOptions topts;
  topts.interpolate(false).type(kScalar);
  pmb->exchange(tvars, topts);

  BoundaryFuncOptions bops;
  bops.nghost(pmb->pcoord->options->nghost());
  bops.type(kScalar);
  for (int i = 0; i < pmb->options->bfuncs().size(); ++i) {
    if (pmb->options->bfuncs()[i] == nullptr) continue;
    pmb->options->bfuncs()[i](theta, 3 - i / 2, bops);
  }
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` | both arms conserve every tracer across the +X/+Y seam; the limiter fires; the hat stays in $[0,1]$ | $10^{-13}$ drift; $-10^{-15}$ to $1+10^{-5}$ | `DRIFT_TOL` and bounds in the script |
| `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_moist_python` | the same with moist species | as above | in the script |
| `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam` | a two-process $x_1$ seam with sedimentation and the limiter keeps mass | in the test | @sec-ch03-x1seams |

: Tests of the donor-factor copy. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-thetacopy-tests}

The seam test places the downwind edge of a tracer hat on the +X/+Y seam so that $\Theta$ jumps there, and checks the bounds and
`DRIFT_TOL` ({{< code tests/test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere.py main >}},
{{< code tests/test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere.py DRIFT_TOL >}}). How large the leak of an interpolated fill
would be is not measured at the pin. The same script also runs as `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_cov_off_python`
and `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_flux_covariance_python`, with the deck key `dynamics.flux-covariance` set to
false and true by the script's `--flux-covariance` argument ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). Both Python tests
have CUDA twins (`_cuda_python`) registered when CUDA is built; the sedimentation test runs on two processes. At the
pin the three tests of the table pass, with the CUDA twins on a GPU.[^tc-run]

### Limits

The corner ghosts of $\Theta$ are synthesised by `fill_corners` (@sec-ch03-exchange) and are not any cell's factor; a
corner cell is never the donor of a face whose flux the block updates with (read from the code; not measured). The
raw copy and the bfunc fill apply the no-op `custom` bfunc at panel edges (@sec-ch03-physfaces). The switch
combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
